compare__authoredup.title: Signal vs AuthoredUp: what to write vs how to format it
compare__authoredup.description: Signal vs AuthoredUp compared honestly: features, pricing and who each tool fits. AuthoredUp formats what you write. Signal helps you decide what to say.

faqs.q: Can Signal and AuthoredUp be used together?
faqs.a: Yes, and many professionals do exactly that. Signal solves the ideation stage each morning; you then paste the structured draft into LinkedIn's composer and use AuthoredUp to format, preview and refine it before publishing.

faqs.q: Do I need both tools, or just one?
faqs.a: Most people only need one at a time. If the blank page is the problem, start with Signal. If you already know what to write and want sharper formatting and hook scoring, start with AuthoredUp, then add the second tool once the first bottleneck is solved.

faqs.q: Is AuthoredUp's free plan enough to get started?
faqs.a: AuthoredUp's free plan covers limited post saves and basic formatting, which is enough to test the editor properly. Full access to analytics, hook scoring and unlimited drafts starts at around $12/month.

faqs.q: Will AuthoredUp help me figure out what to write about?
faqs.a: No, AuthoredUp is a post editor and analytics tool: it improves posts you've already drafted rather than generating topic ideas. For the ideation stage, a tool like Signal is built specifically for that gap.

faqs.q: Is Signal a good Kleo alternative?
faqs.a: Yes, especially for professionals who want to write in their own voice rather than have AI draft for them. Signal starts with a research-backed question, you answer it, and it structures your answer into a post. It costs £35 a month with a 7-day free trial, against Kleo 3.0's $99 a month with no trial.

faqs.q: Why did Kleo's extension shut down, and does that affect me?
faqs.a: LinkedIn issued a cease-and-desist over the original extension, which overlaid and read LinkedIn's interface. Kleo complied and rebuilt as the Kleo 3.0 web app, so the current product no longer carries that account risk. It does mean you now draft in Kleo's app and switch to LinkedIn to publish.

faqs.q: How much does Kleo cost compared to Signal?
faqs.a: Kleo 3.0 runs on a single plan at $99 a month, or $999 a year, with no free trial and a 30-day money-back guarantee. Signal is £35 a month with a 7-day free trial.

faqs.q: Which is better for a consultant or founder?
faqs.a: Signal is built for consultants, founders and fractional executives who sell on credibility. It starts from your own expertise rather than a swipe file or template, so posts sound like you. Kleo suits prolific solo creators who want AI to draft at volume.

faqs.q: Is Signal a direct replacement for Taplio?
faqs.a: Not exactly, because the two tools solve different problems for different audiences. Taplio is a content-generation tool built for high-volume drafting and sales teams, while Signal is a thinking tool built for ideation. If your bottleneck is knowing what to post, Signal solves that; if you need a viral post library, scheduling and a lead database, Taplio's feature set is built for exactly that.

faqs.q: Why does Taplio's AI-generated content sometimes get flagged as templated?
faqs.a: LinkedIn's 2026 algorithm identifies formulaic, AI-generated content and reduces its reach by up to 47%. Taplio drafts from a short prompt, which can produce posts that read as generic unless they're heavily edited afterwards.

faqs.q: Is Taplio worth it for a solo consultant?
faqs.a: It depends on where your actual bottleneck sits. Taplio's AI features that matter most sit at the $65/month tier, which is a significant cost for someone posting three times a week. Solo consultants whose real blocker is ideation rather than drafting speed are often better served by a cheaper, ideation-first tool.

faqs.q: Can I switch from Taplio to Signal without losing my content history?
faqs.a: Yes. Signal doesn't import your Taplio drafts, but it doesn't need to. Each morning it gives you a new research-backed question to answer in your own words, so you start fresh with content grounded in what your market is discussing that day.
